question: What happened to US inflation during 2025, according to the consumer price index?
text:
U.S. inflation **eased slightly overall in 2025, but it didn’t fall steadily**. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose **2.7% from December 2024 to December 2025**, compared with **2.9%** over the previous 12 months. Prices were still rising, just a bit more slowly. ([bls.gov](https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/consumer-price-index-2025-in-review.htm?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block))

Year-over-year inflation started at **3.0% in January**, fell to **2.3% in April**, climbed back to **3.0% in September**, and ended the year at **2.7%**. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not publish an October CPI reading because of the federal government shutdown. ([bls.gov](https://www.bls.gov/regions/mid-atlantic/data/consumerpriceindexhistorical_us_table.htm?utm_source=openai))

**Core CPI**, which excludes food and energy, rose **2.6%** over the year. Food prices rose **3.1%**, and shelter prices rose **3.2%**. ([bls.gov](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_01132026.htm))
